parsed.rationale: The structural evidence explicitly shows `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, meaning these two protocols share no overlapping members. `HLSAVPlayerProtocol` exposes low-level AVFoundation primitives (`currentTime`, `rate`, `seekableTimeRanges`, `seek:(to time: CMTime)`) while `TimeShiftablePlayer` exposes a higher-level domain API (`secondsBehindLive`, `isAtLiveEdge`, `stateStream`, `eventStream`, `makeAudioBufferStream`). The only superficial overlap is the bare `play:()` method name, but the two protocols encode distinct abstraction layers — one wraps AVPlayer internals and the other models a time-shifting radio player — so a forced inheritance relationship would couple unrelated concerns. The coincidence of both being in the `Playback` package and both being `interface` kinds at line 20 is structural noise, not semantic alignment.
